bull_bear.body:
- Decades of accumulated domain expertise in building mission-critical technology platforms for financial markets, regulators and enterprises, now being redeployed into new segments
- Incumbent exchange-technology supplier to Metropolitan Stock Exchange of India Ltd., supporting large trading volumes
- Regulator-facing position in regulatory technology: platform adopted by the Regulator of Housing Finance Companies, with half a dozen HFCs onboarded during FY26, described by management as growing market acceptance
- Large treasury/investment base and shareholders' funds, with the Board's identified core competencies centred on treasury management, banking and investments
- Ongoing in-house R&D spend recognised in the accounts (₹ 1,047.25 lakhs in FY26 revenue expenditure on research and development)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Litigation and regulatory overhang from the legacy NSEL matter, spanning the Company and its subsidiaries — The Directors' Report and notes describe a civil suit by L.J. Tanna, ED proceedings and cross appeal, NCLT/NCLAT orders that led the MCA to appoint three Nominee Directors (stayed by the Supreme Court in March 2022 and kept in abeyance by order dated 13 April 2026), and the NSEL one-time settlement scheme with 5,682 traders which management only says it is confident will go through as sanctioned by the NCLT. The outcome is not in the Company's control.
- Attachment of liquid assets under the MPID Act and PMLA constrains liquidity and the deployment of the treasury — The standalone risk-management note states explicitly that certain liquid assets are attached under the MPID Act and PMLA Act, resulting in some constraint on liquidity, and the interest-rate note cross-refers to a separate note on attachment of investments. The Company is predominantly equity financed with no borrowings, so the treasury is the main earnings engine - its encumbrance is structural, not incidental.
- Court-imposed inability to distribute dividends despite shareholder approval — The Bombay High Court order of September 30, 2015 directs that no dividend be distributed pending disposal of the Notice of Motion, leaving dividends approved for FY2014-15 and for FY2016-17 through FY2024-25 undistributed and the FY2025-26 recommendation conditional on a judicial order. Cash returns to shareholders are therefore outside management's control.
- Customer and revenue concentration in the operating businesses — The Exchange Technology division is described as continuing to serve Metropolitan Stock Exchange of India Ltd. as its client, with one newly onboarded Market Place technology client; Risk Solutions depends heavily on a small number of regulators and the Regulator of Housing Finance Companies. The BRSR also records investments in related parties at 73.61% of total investments made. A narrow counterparty base makes revenue vulnerable to the loss of a single relationship.
- Credit risk on trade receivables and on specific distressed investment exposures — The Company runs an expected-credit-loss model on ageing receivables and fully provides the more-than-270-day bucket; the risk note specifically cross-refers to investments in Non-Convertible Debentures of IL&FS Transport Networks Ltd and Perpetual Bonds of Yes Bank Limited. At subsidiary level, IBMA states the recoverability of trade debts and other receivables has been impacted by the abrupt closure of its business and loss of credibility, and has made full provision.
- Price risk on a large investment book carried at fair value — The Company states it is mainly exposed to price risk through investments in debt mutual funds, whose future market values are uncertain, and relies on internal policies and guidelines to minimise it. With the business predominantly equity financed and a substantial part of income arising from interest and fair-value movements, reported results are sensitive to market levels rather than to operations alone.
- Auditor qualifications at the Company and at subsidiary NSEL, including non-provisioning against recoverable amounts — The Directors' Report carries an explanation to qualifications in the Auditors' Report dated May 18, 2026, including qualifications raised by NSEL's statutory auditors that were reproduced in the consolidated report, and notes the Company provided for the majority of values or disclosed the reason for non-provisioning while stating it is making full efforts for recovery. An unresolved qualification is a standing question over carrying values.
- Contingent liabilities and criminal/tax proceedings concentrated in the NSEL and IBMA subsidiaries — Disclosed matters include an FIU-India penalty under appeal, service-tax and income-tax demands carried as contingent liabilities with no provision because the entities are confident of favourable orders, MPID Special Case proceedings, a PMLA prosecution complaint, an SFIO complaint and multiple recovery suits against IBMA. These sit inside subsidiaries the group consolidates, and the consolidated result is loss-making while the standalone entity is profitable.
- Execution risk in the pivot to new technology verticals, where material loss-making subsidiaries carry the build-out — The growth narrative rests on early-stage ventures - 63SATS (CYBX, CSF, Cyberdome), Ticker and its step-down subsidiaries, QiLegal - rather than on the established exchange-technology base, and several of the named carrier entities reported losses for the year. The reports describe products, platforms and development work in progress, so the revenue is prospective rather than demonstrated.

business.body: The company develops and operates mission-critical technology platforms for financial markets, regulators, enterprises and, increasingly, individual consumers. Its Exchange Technology division supplies marketplace and exchange technology (its named client being Metropolitan Stock Exchange of India Ltd.), Risk Solutions supplies enterprise regulatory-data and risk-computation software to regulators, central banks, housing finance institutions and the wider BFSI sector, QiLegal is an integrated LegalTech platform for India's legal ecosystem, and cybersecurity is delivered through the subsidiary 63SATS Cybertech Limited. outlook.body:
- Transform into a technology-led enterprise focused on securing the digital economy, under the FY26 theme "Securing Digital Life"
- Build out 63SATS (subsidiary) as an umbrella cybersecurity offering across three layers - individual, enterprise and government - with CYBX for direct-to-consumer mobile security, Cyber Security Force (CSF) for enterprises and Cyberdome for critical public infrastructure
- Advance capability across Web3, Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain, LegalTech and Cybersecurity, described by management as the critical domains where 2025-26 saw significant advancement
- Expand operations both with current tools and by acquiring new technological advancements, and by adopting newer technologies in existing operations and upcoming ventures
- Deepen the regulatory-technology footprint in Risk Solutions by positioning DataCollector/Riskalculator-type platforms as the backbone for regulators, central banks, housing finance institutions and the wider BFSI sector
- Leverage existing exchange-technology talent and proven platforms into newer market segments beyond the Metropolitan Stock Exchange of India relationship, including Market Place technology software
- Develop QiLegal as an integrated cloud-based, AI-enabled LegalTech platform to modernise India's legal ecosystem
- Portfolio pruning: the sale of the STP Gate Business Undertaking was completed on a slump-sale basis on September 09, 2025, and the voluntary liquidation of IBS Forex Ltd. remains to be completed
- Resolve the NSEL legacy through the NCLT-sanctioned one-time settlement scheme with 5,682 traders
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report describes expansion in platform and footprint terms rather than physical capacity; 63 moons states it does not manufacture any products and describes itself as a service (Information Technology) business. During FY 2025-26 the Company says it continued to strengthen its technological capabilities while expanding the digital infrastructure underpinning its business, and that it is expanding operations with current tools and by acquiring new technological advancements. The concrete expansion steps named are: build-out of the cybersecurity portfolio through subsidiary 63SATS Cybertech Limited across three layers (CYBX for direct-to-consumer mobile security, Cyber Security Force for enterprises, Cyberdome for critical public infrastructure); onboarding of a new Market Place technology software client in the Exchange Technology division, which generated incremental revenue, with the division stating it is exploring and expanding opportunities for 2025-26 and beyond; onboarding of half a dozen Housing Finance Companies onto the Risk Solutions regulatory data submission platform plus delivery of a Securitization Data Capture Module and a Comparison Module for the HFC regulator; an NLP-based Business Intelligence utility and a BRSR / BRSR-core application still under development; and continued evolution of the QiLegal cloud LegalTech platform. On the portfolio side, the sale of the STP Gate Business Undertaking was completed on September 09, 2025 on a slump-sale basis after fulfilment of all Conditions Precedent, Ticker Limited incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary during the year, Quantblock Technovation Private Limited (formerly 9Point Capital Private Limited) became a subsidiary of Ticker Limited with effect from 09.05.2025, and the voluntary liquidation of IBS Forex Ltd. is yet to be completed. The report discloses no rupee capex quantum and no installed capacity. BRSR Principle 2 records R&D and capex investment in technologies to improve environmental and social impacts as Nil for both the current and previous financial year.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Accelerating digital adoption across industries and everyday life is the stated basis for building technology platforms that combine innovation with resilience
- Management frames cybersecurity demand as arising because digital security has become an essential layer of everyday digital life and the threat landscape is increasingly sophisticated
- In Risk Solutions, management cites onboarding of half a dozen Housing Finance Companies onto the regulator's data submission platform as evidence of growing market acceptance
- In Exchange Technology, management attributes incremental revenue to the successful onboarding of a new client for Market Place technology software and describes this as momentum to build on
- Evolving regulatory priorities on sustainability and governance are cited as the driver for developing a BRSR / BRSR-core application
- Management states it is confident the NSEL one-time settlement will go through as approved by the NCLT, with support from the Central and State Government - a management claim, not an outcome

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Accelerating digital adoption across industries and everyday life is the stated basis for building technology platforms that combine innovation with resilience
- Management frames cybersecurity demand as arising because digital security has become an essential layer of everyday digital life and the threat landscape is increasingly sophisticated
- In Risk Solutions, management cites onboarding of half a dozen Housing Finance Companies onto the regulator's data submission platform as evidence of growing market acceptance
- In Exchange Technology, management attributes incremental revenue to the successful onboarding of a new client for Market Place technology software and describes this as momentum to build on
- Evolving regulatory priorities on sustainability and governance are cited as the driver for developing a BRSR / BRSR-core application
- Management states it is confident the NSEL one-time settlement will go through as approved by the NCLT, with support from the Central and State Government - a management claim, not an outcome

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Transform into a technology-led enterprise focused on securing the digital economy, under the FY26 theme "Securing Digital Life"
- Build out 63SATS (subsidiary) as an umbrella cybersecurity offering across three layers - individual, enterprise and government - with CYBX for direct-to-consumer mobile security, Cyber Security Force (CSF) for enterprises and Cyberdome for critical public infrastructure
- Advance capability across Web3, Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain, LegalTech and Cybersecurity, described by management as the critical domains where 2025-26 saw significant advancement
- Expand operations both with current tools and by acquiring new technological advancements, and by adopting newer technologies in existing operations and upcoming ventures
- Deepen the regulatory-technology footprint in Risk Solutions by positioning DataCollector/Riskalculator-type platforms as the backbone for regulators, central banks, housing finance institutions and the wider BFSI sector
- Leverage existing exchange-technology talent and proven platforms into newer market segments beyond the Metropolitan Stock Exchange of India relationship, including Market Place technology software
- Develop QiLegal as an integrated cloud-based, AI-enabled LegalTech platform to modernise India's legal ecosystem
- Portfolio pruning: the sale of the STP Gate Business Undertaking was completed on a slump-sale basis on September 09, 2025, and the voluntary liquidation of IBS Forex Ltd. remains to be completed
- Resolve the NSEL legacy through the NCLT-sanctioned one-time settlement scheme with 5,682 traders

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The annual report describes expansion in platform and footprint terms rather than physical capacity; 63 moons states it does not manufacture any products and describes itself as a service (Information Technology) business. During FY 2025-26 the Company says it continued to strengthen its technological capabilities while expanding the digital infrastructure underpinning its business, and that it is expanding operations with current tools and by acquiring new technological advancements. The concrete expansion steps named are: build-out of the cybersecurity portfolio through subsidiary 63SATS Cybertech Limited across three layers (CYBX for direct-to-consumer mobile security, Cyber Security Force for enterprises, Cyberdome for critical public infrastructure); onboarding of a new Market Place technology software client in the Exchange Technology division, which generated incremental revenue, with the division stating it is exploring and expanding opportunities for 2025-26 and beyond; onboarding of half a dozen Housing Finance Companies onto the Risk Solutions regulatory data submission platform plus delivery of a Securitization Data Capture Module and a Comparison Module for the HFC regulator; an NLP-based Business Intelligence utility and a BRSR / BRSR-core application still under development; and continued evolution of the QiLegal cloud LegalTech platform. On the portfolio side, the sale of the STP Gate Business Undertaking was completed on September 09, 2025 on a slump-sale basis after fulfilment of all Conditions Precedent, Ticker Limited incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary during the year, Quantblock Technovation Private Limited (formerly 9Point Capital Private Limited) became a subsidiary of Ticker Limited with effect from 09.05.2025, and the voluntary liquidation of IBS Forex Ltd. is yet to be completed. The report discloses no rupee capex quantum and no installed capacity. BRSR Principle 2 records R&D and capex investment in technologies to improve environmental and social impacts as Nil for both the current and previous financial year.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Decades of accumulated domain expertise in building mission-critical technology platforms for financial markets, regulators and enterprises, now being redeployed into new segments
- Incumbent exchange-technology supplier to Metropolitan Stock Exchange of India Ltd., supporting large trading volumes
- Regulator-facing position in regulatory technology: platform adopted by the Regulator of Housing Finance Companies, with half a dozen HFCs onboarded during FY26, described by management as growing market acceptance
- Large treasury/investment base and shareholders' funds, with the Board's identified core competencies centred on treasury management, banking and investments
- Ongoing in-house R&D spend recognised in the accounts (₹ 1,047.25 lakhs in FY26 revenue expenditure on research and development)

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Litigation and regulatory overhang from the legacy NSEL matter, spanning the Company and its subsidiaries — The Directors' Report and notes describe a civil suit by L.J. Tanna, ED proceedings and cross appeal, NCLT/NCLAT orders that led the MCA to appoint three Nominee Directors (stayed by the Supreme Court in March 2022 and kept in abeyance by order dated 13 April 2026), and the NSEL one-time settlement scheme with 5,682 traders which management only says it is confident will go through as sanctioned by the NCLT. The outcome is not in the Company's control.
- Attachment of liquid assets under the MPID Act and PMLA constrains liquidity and the deployment of the treasury — The standalone risk-management note states explicitly that certain liquid assets are attached under the MPID Act and PMLA Act, resulting in some constraint on liquidity, and the interest-rate note cross-refers to a separate note on attachment of investments. The Company is predominantly equity financed with no borrowings, so the treasury is the main earnings engine - its encumbrance is structural, not incidental.
- Court-imposed inability to distribute dividends despite shareholder approval — The Bombay High Court order of September 30, 2015 directs that no dividend be distributed pending disposal of the Notice of Motion, leaving dividends approved for FY2014-15 and for FY2016-17 through FY2024-25 undistributed and the FY2025-26 recommendation conditional on a judicial order. Cash returns to shareholders are therefore outside management's control.
- Customer and revenue concentration in the operating businesses — The Exchange Technology division is described as continuing to serve Metropolitan Stock Exchange of India Ltd. as its client, with one newly onboarded Market Place technology client; Risk Solutions depends heavily on a small number of regulators and the Regulator of Housing Finance Companies. The BRSR also records investments in related parties at 73.61% of total investments made. A narrow counterparty base makes revenue vulnerable to the loss of a single relationship.
- Credit risk on trade receivables and on specific distressed investment exposures — The Company runs an expected-credit-loss model on ageing receivables and fully provides the more-than-270-day bucket; the risk note specifically cross-refers to investments in Non-Convertible Debentures of IL&FS Transport Networks Ltd and Perpetual Bonds of Yes Bank Limited. At subsidiary level, IBMA states the recoverability of trade debts and other receivables has been impacted by the abrupt closure of its business and loss of credibility, and has made full provision.
- Price risk on a large investment book carried at fair value — The Company states it is mainly exposed to price risk through investments in debt mutual funds, whose future market values are uncertain, and relies on internal policies and guidelines to minimise it. With the business predominantly equity financed and a substantial part of income arising from interest and fair-value movements, reported results are sensitive to market levels rather than to operations alone.
- Auditor qualifications at the Company and at subsidiary NSEL, including non-provisioning against recoverable amounts — The Directors' Report carries an explanation to qualifications in the Auditors' Report dated May 18, 2026, including qualifications raised by NSEL's statutory auditors that were reproduced in the consolidated report, and notes the Company provided for the majority of values or disclosed the reason for non-provisioning while stating it is making full efforts for recovery. An unresolved qualification is a standing question over carrying values.
- Contingent liabilities and criminal/tax proceedings concentrated in the NSEL and IBMA subsidiaries — Disclosed matters include an FIU-India penalty under appeal, service-tax and income-tax demands carried as contingent liabilities with no provision because the entities are confident of favourable orders, MPID Special Case proceedings, a PMLA prosecution complaint, an SFIO complaint and multiple recovery suits against IBMA. These sit inside subsidiaries the group consolidates, and the consolidated result is loss-making while the standalone entity is profitable.
- Execution risk in the pivot to new technology verticals, where material loss-making subsidiaries carry the build-out — The growth narrative rests on early-stage ventures - 63SATS (CYBX, CSF, Cyberdome), Ticker and its step-down subsidiaries, QiLegal - rather than on the established exchange-technology base, and several of the named carrier entities reported losses for the year. The reports describe products, platforms and development work in progress, so the revenue is prospective rather than demonstrated.
